_comment: THE DEMO POLICY — how the escalation path is reached WITHOUT lying in an artifact and WITHOUT a mutating route. It is byte-for-byte the document src/replay/main.ts builds inline, plus ONE screenRule. lookup@1.0.0 stays truthfully read_only on every step; the POLICY rates mutating actions on the MEMBER SEARCH screen as irreversible, and riskHandling.irreversible='confirm' turns that into requires:'human' at policy.ts:130-131. That is precisely the riskDrift case policy.ts:123-124 exists for -- an artifact may never talk its risk DOWN, and here the policy talks it UP. It is kept OUT of the default policy on purpose: scripts/verify-determinism.ts spawns src/replay/main.ts with no flags across three read_only scenarios and compares bytes, so a default that could escalate would put a human turn inside the determinism corpus.
_screen_measured: MEMBER_SEARCH, not MEMBER_RESULTS. MEASURED against the real mock: the gate is evaluated against the screen observed BEFORE the action (executor.ts:235-248 passes observation.screen), and lookup@1.0.0 takes no action while standing on MEMBER_RESULTS -- s02 clicks SUBMIT while still on MEMBER_SEARCH. A MEMBER_RESULTS rule therefore never fires on this capability and the escalation path would be unreachable, which is the one thing this fixture exists to avoid.
